title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Zero‑real Agent Policy (ZAP)

### The Breakthrough
The authors introduce ZAP, a 27B‑parameter vision‑language model pretrained on internet data and fine‑tuned in simulation using supervised learning and GRPO reinforcement. It attains 96.7% success on real‑world manipulation tasks despite never seeing real‑robot data, outperforming prior VLA baselines and matching a larger GPT‑16 Astra model while being 3× faster and 17× cheaper. This shows large pretrained models can bootstrap sim‑to‑real transfer at scale.

### The Caveats
ZAP is evaluated only on a single Franka arm, so cross‑hardware generalization remains unproven.

## Safe Planning for Agile Quadrupeds

### The Breakthrough
The paper presents a real‑time motion‑planning framework that parameterises trajectories as composite Bernstein polynomials, leveraging their convex‑hull property to enforce continuous collision‑free and input‑bounded constraints. Demonstrations on hardware show the quadruped safely navigating among unknown moving obstacles with agile, coupled lateral and heading motions that simplified models miss.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparisons are provided, leaving the magnitude of safety and speed improvements unclear.

## Differentiable Contact Dynamics

### The Breakthrough
A smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact is derived via a central‑path relaxation that is used only in the backward pass, preserving the hard‑contact forward solve. This enables training a legged‑robot policy in under two minutes and transferring it to hardware without fine‑tuning, while also improving contact‑implicit trajectory optimization. Results are shown on a trotting robot handling pushes, debris, and slippery ground.

### The Caveats
The method is validated only on a single trotting robot, so its broader applicability to other gaits or morphologies is unproven.

## FLORE Force‑Reactive Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
FLORE learns force‑reactive loco‑manipulation from robot‑free demonstrations captured with handheld force‑sensing grippers and wearable body trackers; a diffusion‑based policy predicts whole‑body motions and per‑hand force vectors, executed by a hybrid compliance controller. In simulation the approach reaches 80% task success on three contact‑rich scenarios, far exceeding a position‑only baseline.

### The Caveats
All results are confined to simulation; no hardware experiments verify the diffusion policy or hybrid controller on a real humanoid.

## Genie 4 World Simulation

### The Breakthrough
Google’s Genie 4 combines a Gemini‑based reasoning engine with a pixel‑level generator to produce synchronized video, audio, and dialogue in real time, supporting natural‑language scene edits such as weather changes or object insertion. The system is offered as a research preview for trusted testers and is promoted for robot training, content creation, and immersive experiences.

### The Caveats
Claims are supported only by demo videos; there are no quantitative benchmarks, baseline comparisons, or real‑world robot tests.

## MIRA‑AI Waste Detection

### The Breakthrough
MIRA‑AI is an open‑source Python pipeline that trains a compact YOLO11n detector on a curated waste dataset, achieving ~90.6% mAP50 on a 415‑image validation split. It includes live webcam inference, a dashboard, and automated ONNX/TFLite export for edge deployment, aiming to enable automated sorting robots.

### The Caveats
The reported accuracy comes solely from a small validation split; a larger independent test set was never evaluated, leaving performance unverified.

### Priority
ZAP is the best starting point today because it demonstrates near‑perfect real‑world manipulation performance without any real‑robot data, opening a cost‑effective path for many labs.

### One action
Try reproducing ZAP’s simulation‑only fine‑tuning pipeline with a publicly available vision‑language model on your own manipulation tasks.

### What to watch
The legged papers offer complementary advances: the quadruped work focuses on safety‑guaranteed, real‑time planning with continuous‑time collision checks, while the differentiable contact paper provides a rapid‑training gradient that improves policy learning and trajectory optimization. Future research may combine these safety guarantees with differentiable contact to achieve both provable safety and fast, adaptable learning across legged platforms.
